title: 1952 shorts and Symphony in Black
summary: Willard lists Solitude, Sophisticated Lady, VIP Boogie and Symphony in Black; he doesn't recall them or Fredi Washington dancing.

story.theme_name: Jazz musicians in the movies and film scoring
story.community_name: Jazz musicians on film and studio scoring

blocks.x:
I see. Then, again in 1952 -- I guess
they made a whole series in 1952 of those little three minute
shorts, but here's one, "Solitude," and you're playing in the
band; Jimmy Grissom is singing. And another one, at about
the same time, "Sophisticated Lady," three minutes long.

Oh, he did so many things with a lot
of the guys in the band.

But you're here, you're on it.
The other two films, the listings, are one more short, "VIP's
Boogie." Remember when Duke first introduced that? No, were

you in the band then? No, I guess not when he first introduced it; it was originally called "Threesome" -- a number that he later broke in to two parts and called "VIP Boogie" and "Jam with Sam." Remember that?

Another thing is an old one, the film, "Symphony in Black," 1934. It was a short -- nine minutes. They put it on television not ago, and it was Duke's band, with Billie Holliday, and the band at that point was Arthur Whetsob Wetzel, Freddie Jenkins, Cootie Williams, Joe Nance and Lawrence Nanton, Brown, Juan Tizol, Barney Bigard, Johnny Hodges, Otto Hardwick, Harry Carney, Fred Guy, Wellman Braud Wilan Grove, Sonny Greer and Duke. And that was the one that Freddie Washington danced in. Remember making that?
The only time I remember Freddie Washington was at the Apollo Theatre, when we were playing the Apollo Theatre, for a Cotton Club show. Freddie Washington was dancing for Henry Whetsol. "Hyparna."
I see. But you don't remember making a film in Hollywood, a short film of nine minutes called "Symphony in Black?"
He did quite a few of things like that, and it's hard to remember, with different people, you know?
Yeah. But she danced in that one. Because I remember. I've seen it.
Freddie Washington danced while the band was playing -- Duke's band, and you were in it, and Barney does a long solo, and Freddie Washington does a dance.
